headline: Columbia River Gorge Permits and Garden Reservations
reservation: Timed-use permits are required for personal vehicles at Multnomah Falls and certain Waterfall Corridor trailheads during peak summer months. The Portland Japanese Garden suggests advance booking for specific entry windows to manage capacity. Always check the official Oregon State Parks or U.S. Forest Service sites for current permit seasons and pass requirements.

days.title: Urban Forests and Skyline Blooms

stops.name: Forest Park
stops.detail: Hike a segment of the Wildwood Trail to experience a massive temperate rainforest within city limits.

stops.name: International Rose Test Garden
stops.detail: View over 10,000 rose bushes with a backdrop of Mount Hood on clear days.

days.driving: Allow 20–40 minutes via local roads or light rail; conditions vary
days.note: Use the Washington Park shuttle to move between the gardens and the MAX light rail station.

days.title: Cascadia Waterfalls and River Views

stops.name: Multnomah Falls
stops.detail: Witness the 620-foot drop of Oregon's tallest waterfall from the historic Benson Bridge.

stops.name: Vista House at Crown Point
stops.detail: Stop at this historic observatory for a panoramic vista of the Columbia River Gorge.

days.driving: Allow 90–120 minutes for the full loop; conditions vary
days.note: Arrive early at the Gorge to secure parking, as permits do not guarantee a specific space.

days.title: Riverfronts and Literary Landmarks

stops.name: Tom McCall Waterfront Park
stops.detail: Walk or bike the paved paths along the Willamette River, especially scenic during cherry blossom season.

stops.name: Powell’s City of Books
stops.detail: Browse the world's largest independent bookstore, spanning an entire city block.

days.driving: Walking or short local transfers; conditions vary
days.note: Expect larger crowds on weekends at the Saturday Market near the Burnside Bridge.

intel.title: Gorge and Downtown Logistics
intel.text: Multnomah Falls parking lots often close by 10 AM on summer weekends due to congestion. Downtown parking is primarily metered; utilize public transit to avoid high garage fees.

intel.title: Mountain Topography
intel.text: Cellular reception is strong in the city but becomes unreliable once you enter the deep canyons of the Columbia River Gorge. Download trail maps for Forest Park as the dense canopy can interfere with GPS accuracy.

intel.title: Oregon Service
intel.text: Fuel is readily available throughout the metro area and along I-84. Be aware that Oregon law regarding self-service fueling has changed; verify current station policies upon arrival.

intel.title: Seasonal Planning
intel.text: Summer offers the driest trails, while winter is best for viewing powerful waterfall flows. June is the peak for rose blooms, though specific dates vary by annual temperature.

intel.title: Trail Conditions
intel.text: Winter storms can cause seasonal closures on the Historic Columbia River Highway and Waterfall Corridor trails. Always check the TripCheck portal for real-time road and pass information.

plan.arrival: Collect vehicle at PDX, follow I-84 West for 20 minutes to reach the city center, and stop in the Pearl District for supplies.
plan.vehicle: Compact cars are ideal for city streets; carry traction devices if driving toward Mount Hood in winter.
plan.goldenHour: Pittock Mansion provides a classic sunset viewpoint overlooking the city and Mount Hood, though the grounds have specific closing hours.
